question.text: Mr. Prakash Nair wishes to invest in Tapti Infrastructure Fund (Category II, non-AI) jointly with his wife Ms. Leela Nair. They have combined surplus of INR 1.2 crore. Which of the following is CORRECT?

answer.text: They cannot invest jointly; each must independently meet INR 1 crore minimum
Joint investment is permitted between spouses (or parent-child / parent-parent) with combined INR 1 crore min; not more than 2 persons may act as joint investors
Three or more joint investors may pool to meet the INR 1 crore floor
Minimum for joint investment is INR 5 crore regardless of relationship

explanation.text: The Logic: Per SEBI Circular No. CIR/IMD/DF/14/2014 and AIF Regulations: an AIF can accept joint investors where the relationship is (a) investor and spouse, (b) investor and parent, or (c) investor and son/daughter. NOT more than 2 PERSONS may act as joint investors. Minimum investment of INR 1 crore applies to the joint holding (not each person). For any OTHER joint-investor combinations, the INR 1 crore minimum applies per investor individually. This requirement does not apply to Accredited Investors. The Trap: Option A ignores the joint-investor carve-out. Option C allows 3+ which breaches the 2-person cap. Option D invents INR 5 crore. Cross-Exam Context: XIX-C tests joint-investor rules. XXI-A/B PMS have their own joint-account rules. AI framework supersedes the INR 1 crore floor for accredited joint holders.
